newsitem.title: UK: MOSVOLD SAYS Q2 PRE-TAX LOSS $1.475 MLN.
newsitem.headline: MOSVOLD SAYS Q2 PRE-TAX LOSS $1.475 MLN.

text.p: Mosvold Shipping ASA, a Norwegian tanker owner, has reported a second quarter pre-tax loss of $1.475 million against a pre-tax profit of $0.314 million in the same period a year earlier.
Mosvold said on Tuesday the figures reflected costs of $1.6 million linked to its recent acquisition of two further VLCCs, Mosking and Mosqueen.
Gross operating income for the three months to the end of June increased to $6.169 million from $3.540 million, reflecting the expansion of Mosvold's fleet.
Mosvold president Magne Kristiansen told Reuters: "The quarter has been as we expected. The tanker charter market is very strong, which gives us confidence for the remainder of this year."
Mosvold said that average daily timecharter income for its first pair of VLCCs, Moscliff and Mosocean was $15,800 per day in the second quarter, up from $14,400 per day in the first quarter.
Over the first half of the year, average daily timecharter income was $15,100, compared with $15,400 in the first half of 1996.

Mosvold said it incurred a pre-tax loss of $1.647 million in the first six months of this year, compared with a pre-tax profit of $0.345 million a year earlier. Gross operating income increased to $12.380 million from $7.181 million.
"The company expects the market to remain strong for the remainder of the quarter, and we are also cautiously optimistic about the fourth quarter," Mosvold said.
"The company foresees improvement in the statistical position of VLCC/ULCCs in 1998," it added.
